lines.t: Hello! I'm Leonardo da Vinci. I paint pictures, and before I paint anything, I measure it.
The Duke of Milan wants two panels covered in gold. I need a helper who is good with numbers. That's you!
Hmm. What do you think?
It does look that way. The strip is very long. But it's also very thin.
Interesting! The square is short, but it's much wider than the strip.
Maybe! We'll have to check.
Good. "Not sure yet" is a fine place to start.
Look at the tags. The strip's length is in feet and inches. The gold sheets are in inches.
Let's count the gold for each panel. Then we'll know for sure.
Five sheets? Hmm. Look at the lid. Then look at the note.
Your times table is right, my friend. But something else is not.
I think I see it. Do you?
Because you measured, and you put every length in the same unit first.
How long must it be? That is a puzzle for next time.

lines.t: Master Leonardo! The Duke's gold is here. It cost a lot, so we can't waste a single sheet.
The strip is 1 foot 6 inches long. The square is 6 inches on each side. The strip will need way more gold!
Oh, and the strip is 2 inches wide.
Master Leonardo, I measured the lid of the Duke's jewelry box myself. I wrote a note for the gold.
1 times 5 is 5. I'm sure of it!
Master Leonardo! The gold was just right. Not one sheet wasted!
Now the Duke has a new wish. He sent a letter.
